exposure: maternal age (very young, 23-32 years, advanced age)
outcome: eye, ear, face, and neck anomalies
cohort: The study included 31,128 cases with confirmed non-chromosomal congenital anomalies compared to 2,808,345 total live births in Hungary.
finding: The occurrence of non-chromosomal congenital anomalies was lowest between 23 and 32 years of maternal age, with both very young and advanced maternal ages being associated with an increased relative risk for various types of anomalies.
